label: thm:SOP-1d
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:SOP-1d}
For ${\alpha},{\beta} > -1$ and $s \in {\mathbb N}$. The polynomial $J_n^{({\alpha}-s,{\beta}-s)}$ is orthogonal with respect to the
inner product $\left[ \cdot, \cdot \right]_{{\alpha},{\beta}}^{-s}$ and its norm square is given by
$$
 \left[J_n^{({\alpha}-s,{\beta}-s)},J_n^{({\alpha}-s,{\beta}-s)}\right]_{{\alpha},{\beta}}^{-s}
   = \begin{cases}\mu_n &  0 \le n \le s-1 \\   \widehat h_{n-s}^{({\alpha},{\beta})} & n \ge s \end{cases},
$$
where $\mu_n$ comes from \eqref{eq:SOPd=1}, and $\widehat h_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}$ is the norm square of $\widehat P_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}$, which is given in terms of $h_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}$ by
$$
\widehat h_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})} = \frac{2^{{\alpha}+{\beta}+1}}{c_{{\alpha},{\beta}}} \left(A_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}\right)^2 h_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}.
                                                
                                                                                                           
$$
head: environment

label: eq:Jn(a,-s)
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the hypergeometric expression of the Jacobi polynomials,
$$
P_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}(t) = \frac{({\alpha}+1)_n}{n!} {}_2F_1\left(\begin{matrix} -n \,\,\, n+{\alpha}+{\beta}+1\\ {\alpha}+1 \end{matrix}; \frac{1-t}{2} \right)
$$
and the fact that $P_n^{({\alpha},{\beta})}(t) = (-1)^n P_n^{({\beta},{\alpha})}(-t)$. It follows that
\begin{align*}
 &  \int_{-1}^t \frac{(t-u)^{s-1}}{(s-1)!} P_n^{({\alpha}+s,0)}(u) \mathrm{d} u
   = (-1)^n  \int_{-1}^t \frac{(t-u)^{s-1}}{(s-1)!} P_n^{(0, {\alpha}+s)}(-u) \mathrm{d} u \\
  & \qquad\quad = (-1)^n \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(-n)_k (n+{\alpha}+s+1)_k}{k! k!}
   \int_{-1}^t \frac{(t-u)^{s-1}}{(s-1)!} \left(\frac{1+u}{2} \right)^k \mathrm{d} u \\
  & \qquad\quad = \frac{(-1)^n}{s!} (1+t)^s \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(-n)_k (n+{\alpha}+s+1)_k}{k! (s+1)_k}  \left(\frac{1+t}{2} \right)^k \\
  & \qquad\quad = \frac{(-1)^n}{s!} (1+t)^s \frac{n!}{(s+1)_n} P_n^{(s,{\alpha})}(-t)
     =   \frac{n!}{(n+s)!}  (1+t)^sP_n^{({\alpha},s)}(t).
 \end{align*}
Replacing $n$ by $n-s$ and using $A_n^{({\alpha},s)} = A_n^{({\alpha}+s,0)}$, the identity \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)} then follows from
\eqref{eq:CJ}. The second identity follows from the identity \eqref{eq:Jacobi_n<0}.
head: environment

label: thm:Jacobi-DE-V0
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: lem:fD
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The identity \eqref{eq:fD1} is an immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:fD0}. Moreover, \eqref{eq:fD_basis} follows from the well-known 
formula for the derivative of the Jacobi polynomials, as
\begin{align*}
 \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \left[ P_{n-m}^{(2m + {\beta} + d-1,{\gamma})} (1-2t)\right] Y_\ell^m (\xi) 
   & = \tau_{n,m} P_{n-m-1}^{(2m + {\beta} + d,{\gamma}+1)} (1-2t) Y_\ell^m (x) \\& = \tau_{n,m} {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)}(x,t),
\end{align*}
which also holds for $m=n$, since the above derivative is zero when $n-m=0$.
head: environment

label: thm:partialP
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:partialP}
For ${\beta} > -d$ and ${\gamma} > -1$, let $f$ be a differentiable function such that $f\in L^2({\mathbb V}_0^{d+1}, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},{\gamma}})$
and ${\mathfrak D} f \in  L^2({\mathbb V}_0^{d+1}, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1})$. Then, for $n =0,1,2,\ldots$,
$$
   {\mathfrak D} \operatorname{proj}_n^{{\beta},{\gamma}} f(x,t) = \operatorname{proj}_{n-1}^{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1} \partial_t f (x,t).
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lem:fD}, ${\mathfrak D} \operatorname{proj}_n^{{\beta},{\gamma}} f \in {\mathcal V}_{n-1}^d({\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1})$. Consequently, it follows that
\begin{align*}
& \left \langle  {\mathfrak D} f, {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)}\right \rangle_{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1}  =
  \left \langle {\mathfrak D} \operatorname{proj}_n^{{\beta},{\gamma}} f,  {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)} \right \rangle_{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1}  \\
  & \qquad\qquad = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \sum_{\nu} \hat f_{k,\nu}^{n,({\beta},{\gamma})}  \tau_{n,k}  \left \langle{\mathsf S}_{k,\nu}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)},
        {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)} \right \rangle_{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1}  \\
  &  \qquad\qquad = \tau_{n,m}  \hat f_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},{\gamma})} h_{n-1,m}^{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1},
\end{align*}
which implies immediately that
$$
    \widehat{{\mathfrak D} f}_{m,\ell}^{n-1, ({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)} = \tau_{n,m} \hat f_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},{\gamma})}, \quad 0 \le m \le n-1.
$$
Consequently, we obtain
\begin{align*}
  {\mathfrak D} \operatorname{proj}_n^{{\beta},{\gamma}} f (x,t)
      \, & = \sum_{m=0}^{n-1} \sum_\ell \hat f_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},{\gamma})}\tau_{n,m} {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)}(x,t) \\
       & = \sum_{m=0}^{n-1} \sum_\ell \widehat{{\mathfrak D} f}_{m,\ell}^{n-1, ({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)} {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1)}(x,t) \\
       & = \operatorname{proj}_{n-1}^{{\beta}+1,{\gamma}+1} {\mathfrak D} f (x,t),
\end{align*}
where in the first step we used again ${\mathfrak D}_t {\mathsf S}_{n,\ell}^n(x,t) = 0$.
head: environment

label: cor:approxQ
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:approxQ}
Let ${\beta} > -d$ and ${\gamma} > -1$. Let $r$ be a postive integer and let $f \in C^r({\mathbb V}_0^{d+1})$ such that
 ${\mathfrak D}^k f \in  L^p({\mathbb V}_0^{d+1}, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+k,{\gamma}+k})$ for $0 \le k \le r$.  Then, for $1 \le p \le \infty$,
$$
  \left \| {\mathfrak D}^k f - {\mathfrak D}^k Q_{n,\eta}^{({\beta},{\gamma})}f\right \|_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+k,{\gamma}+k} } \le c_k
      E_{n-k} ({\mathfrak D}^k f)_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+k,{\gamma}+k} }, \qquad 0 \le k \le r.
$$
head: environment

label: eq:wtQ
title: Proof
body_md:
This follows immediately from
\begin{align*}
   {\mathfrak D}^k Q_{n,\eta}^{({\beta},{\gamma})} f & =   \sum_{j=0}^{2n} \eta\left(\frac j n \right)  {\mathfrak D}^j\operatorname{proj}_j^{{\beta},{\gamma}} f
       =   \sum_{j=k}^{2n} \eta\left(\frac j n \right) \operatorname{proj}_{j-k}^{{\beta}+k,{\gamma}+k} f \\
      & =   \sum_{j=0}^{2n-k} \eta\left(\frac {j+k}n \right) \operatorname{proj}_{j}^{{\beta}+k,{\gamma}+k}  {\mathfrak D}^k f
         = {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{({\beta}+k,{\gamma}+k)}  {\mathfrak D}^k  f,
\end{align*}
where we define
\begin{equation} \label{eq:wtQ}
  {\mathsf Q}_{ n,\eta}^{({\beta},{\gamma})} g =  \sum_{j=0}^{2n-k} \eta\left(\frac {j+k}n \right) \operatorname{proj}_{j}^{{\beta},{\gamma}} g, \quad 0 \le k < 2n.
\end{equation}
For fixed $k \le r$ independent of $n$, the function $\eta\left(\frac {j+k}n \right)$ plays essentially the same role
as $\eta\left(\frac {j}n \right)$, so that \eqref{eq:Qn-etaEstimate} holds with ${\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{({\beta},{\gamma})} {\mathfrak D}^k f$ in place
of $Q_{n,\eta}^{({\beta},{\gamma})}f$, form which the proof follows readily.
head: environment

label: thm:SOP-cone
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:SOP-cone}
Let $s \in {\mathbb N}$ and ${\beta} > -d-s$. The polynomials ${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)}$, $1 \le \ell \le \dim {\mathcal H}_m^d$
and $0\le m \le n$ consist of a basis of ${\mathcal V}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{{\beta},-s})$. Moreover, for all $\ell$, ${\mathsf h}_{m,n}^{({\beta},-s)}  =
\langle {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)}, {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)} \rangle_{{\beta},-s}$ satisfies
$$
 {\mathsf h}_{m,n}^{({\beta},-s)}   = \begin{cases}2^{2n-2m} {\lambda}_{n-m} &  0 \le n -m \le s-1, \\
      2^{s - {\beta}-2m-d}\, \widehat h_{n-m-s}^{(s+2m+{\beta}+d-1,0)} & n-m \ge s. \end{cases}
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $q_{n-m}(t) = J_{n-m}^{(2m+{\beta}+d-1, -s)}(t)$. Changing variable $x = t \xi$ and using \eqref{eq:fD_basis}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 \left \langle {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)}, {\mathsf S}_{m',\ell'}^{n',({\beta},-s)} \right \rangle_{{\beta},-s}
  = \, & 2^{ 2s}  \int_0^1 t^{d-1} q_{n-m}^{(s)} (1-2t) q_{n'-m'}^{(s)}(1-2t) t^{{\beta}+s+m+m'} \mathrm{d} t \\
 &\qquad \times  \frac{1}{{\omega}_d} \int_{{\mathbb S}^{d-1}}  Y_\ell^m (\xi)Y_{\ell'}^{m'} (\xi) \mathrm{d} \sigma (\xi) \\
 & + \sum_{k=0}^{s-1} {\lambda}_k 2^{2k} q_{n-m}^{(k)}(-1) q_{n'-m'}^{(k)}(-1)  \\
 &\qquad \times  \frac{1}{{\omega}_d} \int_{{\mathbb S}^{d-1}}    Y_\ell^m (\xi)Y_{\ell'}^{m'} (\xi) \mathrm{d} \sigma (\xi).
\end{align*}
Using the orthogonality of $Y_\ell^m$ and changing the variable $t \mapsto (1-t)/2$ in the first integral, we
see that the expression containing $q_{n-m}$ can be written in terms of the Sobolev inner product
$[\cdot,\cdot]_{{\alpha},{\beta}}^{-s}$ defined in \eqref{eq:SOPd=1}. More precisely, we obtain
$$
\left \langle {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)},  {\mathsf S}_{m',\ell'}^{n',({\beta},-s)} \right \rangle_{{\beta},-s} =
   2^{2 s - {\alpha}-1} [q_{n-m}, q_{n'-m}]_{{\alpha},0}^{-s} \delta_{m,m'} \delta_{\ell,\ell'},
$$
where ${\alpha} = s+{\beta}+2m+d-1$ and the inner product $[\cdot, \cdot]_{{\alpha},0}^{-s}$ is defined as in \eqref{eq:SOPd=1}
but with $\mu_k = 2^{2k} {\lambda}_k/2^{2 s-{\alpha}-1}$. As shown in Theorem \ref{thm:SOP-1d}, the polynomials $J_n^{({\alpha}-s,-s)}$
are orthogonal with respect to this inner product, regardless of the values of $\mu_k$. This
proves the orthogonality of ${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)}$. Moreover,  the norm ${\mathsf h}_{m,n}^{({\beta},-s)}$ follows
from the norm given in Theorem \ref{thm:SOP-1d}.
head: environment

label: cor:der_sS
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $m \le n-s$, by \eqref{eq:fD_basis} and the identity \eqref{eq:CJ1a},
\begin{align*}
{\mathfrak D}^s {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)}(x,t)  \,&  =
     \frac{\mathrm{d}^s}{\mathrm{d} t^s}\left[J_{n-m}^{(2m+{\beta}+d-1,-s)}(1-2t)\right]Y_\ell^m(x) \\
   & = (-2)^{s} \widehat P_{n-m-s}^{(s+2m+{\beta}+d-1,0)}(1-2t)Y_\ell^m(x),
\end{align*}
from which \eqref{eq:D_sS} follows from \eqref{eq:JacobiJ} and the definition of ${\mathsf S}_{\ell,m}^{n,({\beta}+s,0)}$.
Moreover, since $n-m \ge s$, for $1 \le k \le s-1$ it follows immediately by \eqref{eq:CJ1b} that \eqref{eq:D_sS2}
holds. If $m > n-s$, then the derivative in the identity \eqref{eq:D_sS} is evidently zero since the Jacobi polynomial
in ${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)}$ is of degree $n-m <s$. Moreover, for $1 \le k \le s-1$, \eqref{eq:D_sS2} follows
from \eqref{eq:CJ1b}.
head: environment

label: eq:sS-explicit
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows from the identity \eqref{eq:Jacobi_n<0}, which shows, together with \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)=Pn}, that
$$
  J_{n}^{({\alpha},-s)}(1-2t) = \frac{(-1)^s 2^s}{(-n)_s} A_{n-s}^{({\alpha},s)}(1-t)^s P_{n-s}^{({\alpha},s)}(1-2t)
$$
for $n\ge s$, which implies, with $n$ replaced by $n-m$, the identity \eqref{eq:sS-explicit} when $n - m \ge s$.
For $n -m \le s-1$, \eqref{eq:sS-explicit} follows immediately from the definition of $J_n^{({\alpha},-s)}$ in
\eqref{eq:CJ}. Since $\{Y_\ell^m: 1 \le \ell \le m\}$ is a basis of ${\mathcal H}_n^{d,0}$, the decomposition
\eqref{eq:decompVnd} is an immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:sS-explicit}.
head: environment

label: thm:proj-s=int
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: eq:FourierCoeffs
title: Proof
head: environment

label: cor:proj-partial
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:proj-partial}
Let $s$ be a positive integer. For ${\beta} > -d-s$, let $f$ be a differentiable function such that
${\mathfrak D}^s f \in L^2({\mathbb V}_0^{d+1}, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+s,0})$. Then, for $n  \ge s$,
$$
  {\mathfrak D}^s \operatorname{proj}_n^{{\beta},-s} f(x,t) = \operatorname{proj}_{n-s}^{{\beta}+s,0}\left({\mathfrak D}^s f\right) (x,t).
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Taking the derivative ${\mathfrak D}^s$ of \eqref{eq:proj-s=int}, it follows from \eqref{eq:fD1} that the first term in the right-hand
side is zero, while the second term gives the stated identity.
head: environment

label: thm:errorSOP
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Multiplying \eqref{eq:proj-s=int} by $\eta\left( \frac{k}{n} \right)$ and summing up over $k$ gives an expression
of ${\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{({\beta},-s)} f$. Furthermore, by \eqref{eq:fD0}, the Tylor expansion of $t\rightarrow f(x,t)$ with respect to the $t$
variable at $t =1$, together with its remainder formula, gives 
$$
  f(x,t) = \sum_{m=0}^{s-1} \frac{(t-1)^m}{m!}  {\mathfrak D}^m f(x,1) +
   (-1)^s \int_{t}^{1} \frac{(v-t)^{s-1}}{(s-1)!} {\mathfrak D}^s f (x, v) \mathrm{d} v.
$$
Together, the difference of the two identities gives the error formula for $f -{\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{({\beta},-s)} f$ and completes
the proof.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $f \in W_p^s({\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+s,0})$. Then, for $1 \le p \le \infty$,
$$
   \left \|{\mathfrak D}^s f - {\mathfrak D}^s {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{(\beta, -s)}f \right\|_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+s,0}}
    \le c E_n\left( {\mathfrak D}^s f \right)_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta}+s,0}}.
$$
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
If $f(x,t) = (1-t)^s g(x,t)$, then
$$
   \operatorname{proj}_n^{{\beta},-s} f = (1-t)^s \operatorname{proj}_{n-s}^{{\beta},s} g.
$$
head: environment

label: eq:Fourirer-1
title: Proof
body_md:
By the definition of the ${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)}$, it follows from \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)} that
$$
 {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)} (x,t)= \sigma_{m,n} (1-t)^s {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-s, ({\beta},s)}(x,t), \quad
 \sigma_{m,n} :=  \frac{(n-s-m)!}{(n-m)!} A_{n-m}^{(2m+{\beta}+d-1,0)}.
$$
Expanding $g$ in terms of the Fourier orthogonal series in $L^2({\mathbb V}_0^{d+1}, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},1})$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
 f(x,t) = (1-t)^s g(x,t) \,& = (1-t)^s \sum_{n=0}^\infty \sum_{m=0}^n \sum_\ell \hat g_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},s)}
    {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},s)}(x,t) \\
    & = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \sum_{m=0}^n \sum_\ell \hat g_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},s)}
    \sigma_{n+s,m}^{-1} {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n+s, ({\beta},-s)}(x,t).
\end{align*}
Applying the orthogonality in the Sobolev inner product, it follows immediately that
$$
 \left \langle f,  {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n+s, ({\beta},-s)} \right \rangle_{{\beta},-s} =
  \sigma_{n+1,m}^{-1} \hat g_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},s)} \left \langle
    {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n+s, ({\beta},-s)},  {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n+s, ({\beta},-s)} \right \rangle_{{\beta},-s}, \quad 0 \le m \le n;
$$
in particular, with $n$ replaced by $n-s$, we then obtain
\begin{equation} \label{eq:Fourirer-1}
      \hat f_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)} = \sigma_{n,m}^{-s} \hat g_{m,\ell}^{n-s,({\beta},s)}, \quad 0 \le m \le n-s.
\end{equation}
For $n-s < m \le n$, the polynomial $J_{n-m}^{(2m+{\beta}+d-1,-s)}(t)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $s-1$,
so that ${\mathfrak D}^s {\mathsf S}_{n,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-1)}(x,t) = 0$; moreover, ${\mathfrak D}^k f(\xi,1) =0$ for $0 \le k \le s-1$,
since $f$ contains a factor $(1-t)^s$. It follows that $\hat f_{n,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)} = 0$ for $n -s < m \le n$ by the
definition of the Sobolev inner product. Consequently, by \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)} and \eqref{eq:Fourirer-1} we
obtain
\begin{align*}
    (1-t) \operatorname{proj}_{n-s}^{{\beta},s} g\, & = (1-t) \sum_{m=0}^{n-s} \sum_\ell \hat g_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta},s)} {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-s, ({\beta},s)} \\
                   & = \sum_{m=0}^{n} \sum_\ell \hat f_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)} {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, ({\beta},-s)} = \operatorname{proj}_{n}^{{\beta},-s}f.
\end{align*}
The proof is completed.
head: environment

title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $f = (1-t)^s g$, we see that
$$
{\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{(\beta, -1)} f = \sum_{k=0}^{2n} \eta\left( \frac{k}{n}\right) (1-t)^s \operatorname{proj}_{k-1}^{{\beta},s} g
    = (1-t)^s \widetilde {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{\beta,s} g,
$$
where $\widetilde {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{(\beta,s)}$ is defined as in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:approxQ}.
For $p \ge 1$, we then obtain
\begin{align*}
  \left \| f - {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{(\beta, -s)} f \right\|_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},0}}
  & =  \left \| (1-t)^s \left[ g - \widetilde {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{(\beta, s)} g \right] \right\|_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},0}}\\
  & \le \left \|g - \widetilde {\mathsf Q}_{n,\eta}^{(\beta, s)} g \right\|_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},s}} \le c E_n(g)_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},s}},
\end{align*}
By the definition of $E_n(g)_{p, {\mathsf w}}$, it follows immediately $E_n(g)_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},s}} \le E_n(g)_{p, {\mathsf w}_{{\beta},0}}$.
The proof is completed.
head: environment

label: eq:D_gamma
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $k=1$, a quick computation from the definition of ${\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}}$ shows
\begin{align*}
{\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}}[(1-t)  p(t) Y(\xi)]
                                                       
                                                          
                                             
                                                                             
                                             
 =\, & \big((1-t) \left[t(1-t)p''(t) +  [d-1-(d+\gamma+2)t]p'(t)\right] \\
    &  - [d-1-(d+\gamma)t]p(t)\big) Y(\xi)
     + t^{-1}\,(1-t) p(t) \, \Delta_0^{(\xi)}Y(\xi) \\
= \, & (1-t){\mathcal D}_{\gamma+2}[p(t)Y(\xi)] - [d-1-(d+\gamma)t]p(t)Y(\xi),
\end{align*}
which verifies \eqref{eq:D_gamma} for $k=1$. Assume that \eqref{eq:D_gamma} holds for $k\geq 1$.
Then
\begin{align*}
& {\mathcal D}_{\gamma}[(1-t)^{k+1} p(t) Y(\xi)] = {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}} [(1-t)^k (1-t) p(t) Y(\xi)] \\
& \quad = (1-t)^k {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}+2k}[(1-t)p(t) Y(\xi)] \\
&\qquad - k\,(1-t)^{k-1} [d-1-(d+\gamma+k-1)t][(1-t)p(t) Y(\xi)]\\
& \quad =  (1-t)^k \left\{(1-t){\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}+2k+2}[p(t) Y(\xi)] - [d-1-(d+\gamma+2k)t]p(t) Y(\xi)\right\}\\
&\qquad - k\,(1-t)^{k} [d-1-(d+\gamma+k-1)t]p(t) Y(\xi)\\
& \quad = (1-t)^{k+1} {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}+2k+2}[p(t) Y(\xi)] - (k+1)(1-t)^k [d-1-(d+\gamma+k)t]p(t) Y(\xi),
\end{align*}
so that \eqref{eq:D_gamma} holds for $k+1$ and the proof is completed by induction.
head: environment

label: thm:Z
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: eq:Delta0Y
title: Proof
body_md:
Without losing generality, we assume $p$ is a monic polynomial,
$$
p(t) = \sum_{i=0}^j \,(1-t)^i\,a_{j,i}, \quad a_{j,j} = 1.
$$
Our objective is to determine the coefficients $a_{j,i}$ such that $Z_j$ satisfies \eqref{eq:Z}. First, we observe
that \eqref{eq:Z} holds if $p(t) =1$. In this case $Y \in {\mathcal H}_n^{d,0}$ and $Y(x) = t^n Y(\xi)$. Hence, taking
the derivative over $t$ and using the relation \eqref{eq:LB-operator}, a quick computation shows that
\begin{align} \label{eq:Delta0Y}
{\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}} Y(x)= &\, {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}}[t^n Y(\xi)] \\
 = &\, n (n+d-2)Y(\xi) - m (m+{\gamma}+d-1) t^m Y(\xi) + t^{m-1}  \Delta_0 Y(\xi) \notag \\
 =  &\, -m(m+d+{\gamma}-1) t^m Y(\xi) = -m(m+d+{\gamma}-1) Y(x). \notag
\end{align}
For $j \ge 0$, we use the identity \eqref{eq:D_gamma} to obtain
\begin{align*}
& {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}} Z_j(x,t)  =  \sum_{i=0}^j  a_{j,i} {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}}\left[(1-t)^i t^{n-j} Y(\xi)\right] \\
& = \sum_{i=0}^j  a_{j,i} \left[(1-t)^i {\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}+ 2i}[Y(x)] - i(1-t)^{i-1}[d-1-(d+\gamma+i-1)t]  Y(x)\right]
\end{align*}
and then apply \eqref{eq:Delta0Y} for $Y\in {\mathcal H}_{n-j}^{d,0}$ and simplify to obtain
\begin{align*}
{\mathcal D}_{{\gamma}} Z_j(x,t)  =
                                                                                  
                                                                       
                                                                       
\, & \sum_{i=0}^{j} \,(1-t)^i \,a_{j,i} [\lambda_{n-j}^{(\gamma+2i)} - i\,(d+\gamma+i-1)]\,Y(x)\\
&+\sum_{i=0}^{j-1} (i+1)(1-t)^{i}\,(\gamma+i+1) \,a_{j,i+1}\,Y(x)\\
= \,  & (1-t)^j \,\lambda_n^{(\gamma)}\,Y(x) +\sum_{i=0}^{j-1} \,(1-t)^i \\
& \times \{a_{j,i} \,[\lambda_{n-j}^{(\gamma+2i)} - i(d+\gamma+i-1)] + a_{j,i+1}(i+1)(\gamma+i+1)\}Y(x),
\end{align*}
since $a_{j,j} = 1$. Thus, in order to have $Z_{j,n} (x,t)$ satisfying \eqref{eq:Z}, we must have
$$
a_{j,i} \,[\lambda_{n-j}^{(\gamma+2i)} - i(d+\gamma+i-1)] + a_{j,i+1}(i+1)(\gamma+i+1) = a_{j,i} \lambda_n^{(\gamma)}
$$
for $0 \le i \le j-1$, which leads to the recurrence relation
            
   
                                                                                          
   
         
$$
a_{j,i}  = - \frac{(i+1)(\gamma+i+1)}{(j-i)(2n+\gamma+d-1-j+i)}a_{j,i+1} , \quad i=0, 1, \ldots, j-1.
$$
Solving this recurrence relation and using $a_{j,j}  = 1$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{def:a}
a_{j,i} = (-1)^{j-i}\frac{(i+1)_{j-i}(\gamma+i+1)_{j-i}}{(j-i)!(2n+\gamma+d- 1-j+i)_{j-i}}, \quad 0\leq i \leq j.
\end{equation}
                                                                          
Using the identity $(a+i)_{j-i} = (a)_j/(a)_i$ and $(j-i)! = (-1)^i j! / (-j)_i$, we can rewrite it as
$$
 a_{j,i} = (-1)^j c_j \frac{(-j)_i (2n+{\gamma}+d-j-1)_i}{i! ({\gamma}+1)_i}, \quad c_j= \frac{({\gamma}+1)_j}{(2n+{\gamma}+d-j-1)_j},
$$
which is well-defined if $(2n+{\gamma}+d-j-1)_j \ne 0$. Consequently, the polynomial $p$ must be given by
\begin{align*}
 p(x) \,& = (-1)^j c_j
    \phantom{i}_2F_1\left ( \begin{matrix} -j, 2n+{\gamma}+d-j-1 \\ {\gamma}+1 \end{matrix}; 1-t \right) \\
& = (-1)^jc_j P_j^{({\gamma}, 2n-2j+d-2)}(2t-1) =
      c_j P_j^{(2n-2j+d-2, {\gamma})}(1-2t),
\end{align*}
which completes the proof.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $s \in {\mathbb N}$ and $n \in {\mathbb N}_0$. Then the polynomials ${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, (-1,-s)}$ are eigenfunctions
of ${\mathcal D}_{-s}$ if and only if $m \le n-s$ and $m =n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)=Pn}, the polynomials ${\mathsf S}_{m,-\ell}^{n,(-1,-s)}$ can be written as
$$
{\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n,(-1,-s)}(x,y) = c_{n-m} P_{n-m}^{(2m+d-2,-s)}(1-2t) Y_\ell^m(x), \quad n-m \ge s,
$$
so that Theorem \ref{thm:Z} applies for $n - m \ge s$, thus ${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n, (-1,-s)}$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:Z}. If $n = m$, then ${\mathsf S}_{n, \ell}^{n, (-1,-s)}(x,t) = Y_\ell^n(x)$. As a result,
\eqref{eq:Z} holds with $p(z) =1$. For $1 \le n-m \le s-1$, however, the polynomial
$J_{n-m}^{(2m+d-2,-s)}(t) = (1-t)^{n-m}/(n-m)!$ is not the Jacobi polynomial $P_{n-m}^{(2m+d-2,-s)}(t)$,
hence ${\mathsf S}_{n, \ell}^{n, (-1,-s)}$ is not a solution of \eqref{eq:Z}.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
For ${\gamma} = -1$, all elements in ${\mathcal V}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-1})$ are eigenfunctions of ${\mathcal D}_{-1}$; that is,
$$
   {\mathcal D}_{-1} Z = - n  (n+ d-2) Z, \qquad \forall Z \in {\mathcal V}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-1}).
$$
Moreover, the space ${\mathcal V}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-1})$ satisfies a decomposition
$$
{\mathcal V}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-1}) =  {\mathcal H}_n^{d,0} \cup (1-t) {\mathcal V}_{n-1}^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,1}), \qquad n =0,1,\ldots.
$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We only need to prove the decomposition. If $m \le n-1$, it follows from from \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)=Pn} that
${\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-1)}  = c (1-t) {\mathsf S}_{m,\ell}^{n-1,({\beta},1)} \in (1-t) {\mathcal V}_{n-1}^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,1})$, whereas if $m = n$,
then ${\mathsf S}_{n,\ell}^{n,({\beta},-s)} = Y_\ell^n \in {\mathcal H}_n^{d,0}$.
head: environment

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As in the case of $s = 1$, using \eqref{eq:Jn(a,-s)=Pn}, the statement on the eigenspace follows readily
from Theorem \ref{thm:Z}. As it is shown for the dimension of ${\mathcal V}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{{\beta},-s})$, the space
${\mathcal U}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-s})$ has the full dimension $\binom{n+d-1}{d}$ if the Jacobi polynomials
$P_j^{(2n-2j+d-2,-s)}$ does not have the degree reduction, which holds if $2n-j+d-2-s +k =0$ for a
certain integer $k$, $1 \le k \le j$, by \cite[p. 64]{Sz}.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
If $s = 2$, then the space ${\mathcal U}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-2})$ is given by
$$
  {\mathcal U}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-2}) = {\mathcal H}_n^d \cup  \left(1+ (2n+d-4)(1-t) \right) {\mathcal H}_{n-1}^d
   \cup (1-t)^s {\mathcal V}_{n-2}^d ({\mathsf w}_{-1,2})
$$
and it has the full dimension if $-2n-d+5 \ne 1$ or $2n-d+4 \ne 0$ for $n \ge 1$. Thus, ${\mathcal D}_{-2}$ has a complete
basis of polynomials as eigenfunctions if $d$ is odd. In the case that $d$ is even, $ {\mathcal U}_n^d({\mathsf w}_{-1,-2})$ is
not well-defined for $n = d/2-2$.
